summary: Your people did it in your name: {aide} and {appointee} did something to punish {local official} for not backing you, and {reporter} has the emails.
realLife: One life: In 2013 his deputy chief of staff and Port Authority appointees closed bridge lanes into Fort Lee after its mayor did not endorse him. He joked that he worked the cones, then fired her in January 2014, calling her deceitful. Two were convicted in 2016; the Supreme Court overturned the convictions in 2020. Another: As Milwaukee County executive, his chief of staff raised concerns about missing funds from a veterans' fundraiser, and Walker told him to report it to the district attorney. The inquiry convicted people around him, including a former deputy chief of staff.
gates: Staff or appointees acted on record against someone who refused you.
weights: What the record shows you knew.
choices: fire them and say you were lied to
tell your staff to come forward

branches.then: Your line is played back to you when the emails come out.
They are charged, and one says under oath that you lied. You are not charged.

branches.when: an aide stole from a fundraiser
branches.then: Your chief of staff tells you, you tell them to go to the prosecutor, and a long inquiry convicts people near you (C23).

branches.when: the convictions are thrown out years later
branches.then: The highest court overturns them. The damage to you stays.
